framework.name: Careful adoption of agentic AI services
framework.shortName: Careful Adoption of Agentic AI Services
framework.publisher: ASD's ACSC, with CISA, NSA, the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security, NCSC-NZ and NCSC-UK (the 'authoring agencies')
framework.version: May 2026 (no version number; PDF metadata CreationDate 2026-04-30)
framework.idNote: The guidance numbers nothing. Each id is <stage>/<subsection>/<n>: the stage and subsection headings of the 'Recommended best practices' list it sits in, and its position in that list. The text is the PDF's, verbatim.
framework.scope: Every 'Recommended best practices' bullet under 'Best practices for securing agentic AI systems' and 'Defend against future risks', and every Appendix A prerequisite: 140 items. The risk descriptions and the 'Further information' reading list are not controls and are not mapped.
notes: The cyber.gov.au page and PDF (https://www.cyber.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-05/careful_adoption_of_agentic_ai_services.pdf) timed out from this network on 2026-10-09. The text was read from the PDF published by NCSC-NZ, one of the authoring agencies; its metadata names Australian Signals Directorate as author.
CISA's resource page (https://www.cisa.gov/resources-tools/resources/careful-adoption-agentic-ai-services, Publish Date May 01, 2026) links to the cyber.gov.au publication.

The Canadian Centre for Cyber Security's HTML edition (https://cyber.gc.ca/en/guidance/careful-adoption-agentic-ai) uses Canadian spelling and shortens or rewords 51 of the 140 items; the PDF wording is used here.

naKind: 'organisational' is a governance, procurement, staffing, assessment or research activity; 'agent-build' is something done inside the agent itself (its model training, prompts, evaluation, error handling or infrastructure). Neither is a runtime control a third-party tool supplies.

statusMeaning.covered: a shipped mechanism meets the whole recommendation
statusMeaning.partial: a shipped mechanism meets part of it; `limit` says which part
statusMeaning.not-covered: a runtime technical control MoorAI does not provide; `reason` says what is missing
statusMeaning.not-applicable: organisational or agent-build practice, not a runtime tool's job; `naKind` and `reason` say which

catalog.section: Designing secure agents: Controlled context
catalog.text: Structure prompt context using a clear instruction hierarchy to ensure agent behaviour aligns with intended priorities and constraints

catalog.section: Designing secure agents: Controlled context
catalog.text: Implement grounding by providing relevant contextual information using retrieval augmented generation and prompt engineering to mitigate hallucinations and other LLM-related errors

catalog.section: Designing secure agents: Oversight mechanisms
catalog.text: Include mechanisms to facilitate human control and oversight to ensure that agentic AI systems approved for non-sensitive, low-risk tasks cannot autonomously progress into higher-risk activities

catalog.section: Designing secure agents: Oversight mechanisms
catalog.text: Implement human control points throughout the agent workflow, such as live monitoring and interruption during task execution, mandatory human approval for decision-making steps, auditing and reversibility following task execution to ensure security

catalog.section: Designing secure agents: Oversight mechanisms
catalog.text: Define explicit control flows to bound autonomous planning and prevent agents from deviating beyond authorised objectives or actions

catalog.section: Designing secure agents: Identity management
catalog.text: Embed strong identity management mechanisms into agents using manage identity services, decentralised identifiers or public key infrastructure

catalog.section: Designing secure agents: Identity management
catalog.text: Authenticate all inter-agent and agent-to-service API calls using mutual transport layer security to ensure non-repudiation

catalog.section: Designing secure agents: Identity management
catalog.text: Maintain a trusted registry and bind identities to authorised roles; periodically reconcile the registry against the live set of agents

catalog.section: Designing secure agents: Identity management
catalog.text: Deny access for any agent or cryptographic key that is not present in the trusted registry

catalog.section: Designing secure agents: Identity management
catalog.text: Apply role-based identity management and limit agent permissions to the minimum scope required for approved tasks

catalog.section: Designing secure agents: Identity management
catalog.text: Enforce identity-based boundaries to restrict agents’ to authorised actions only

catalog.section: Designing secure agents: Defence in depth
catalog.text: Avoid reliance on a single security mechanism by implementing multiple, overlapping layers of security controls

catalog.section: Designing secure agents: Defence in depth
catalog.text: Apply security controls at all points where information enters or exits the system, including user inputs, tool calls, data pre-processing and model inference

catalog.section: Designing secure agents: Defence in depth
catalog.text: Separate agents for different functions and apply strict boundaries and operational controls to the handoffs from one agent to another

catalog.section: Developing secure agents: Comprehensive testing
catalog.text: Use reward modelling and adversarial testing to detect specification gaming, explicitly incorporating security constraints alongside performance goals

catalog.section: Developing secure agents: Comprehensive testing
catalog.text: Train LLM agents in simulated, controlled environments to learn the implications of actions without causing real security harm

catalog.section: Developing secure agents: Comprehensive testing
catalog.text: Leverage synthetic data generation to create adversarial training examples that reflect real-world operating scenarios

catalog.section: Developing secure agents: Comprehensive testing
catalog.text: Apply active learning to adversarial training scenarios to expose agents to high uncertainty inputs and more efficiently discover unexpected behaviours

catalog.section: Developing secure agents: Appropriate evaluation
catalog.text: Use relevant threat models to define evaluation scenarios, including edge cases beyond typical training conditions

catalog.section: Developing secure agents: Appropriate evaluation
catalog.text: Use techniques, such as Best-of-N sampling (selecting the best output from multiple model responses to the same prompt), multistep reasoning prompts and inference time scaling to draw out the full range of agent behaviours and skills

catalog.section: Developing secure agents: Appropriate evaluation
catalog.text: Evaluate systems across different levels of autonomy to understand performance and risk under changing environmental conditions, including changes in tool, models and resource access, such as web search or code execution

catalog.section: Developing secure agents: Appropriate evaluation
catalog.text: Vary contextual conditions, such as presence or absence of other agents and the timing of evaluation, to understand their impact on task performance

catalog.section: Developing secure agents: Appropriate evaluation
catalog.text: Conduct capability evaluations continuously across the agent development lifecycle

catalog.section: Developing secure agents: Input management
catalog.text: Implement robust input validation and sanitisation for all agent inputs

catalog.section: Developing secure agents: Input management
catalog.text: Integrate prompt injection filters and semantic analysis to detect malicious instructions

catalog.section: Developing secure agents: Input management
catalog.text: Validate context to ensure the system correctly interprets intent before execution

catalog.section: Developing secure agents: Red teaming
catalog.text: Deploy sandbox environments to test agent behaviour before production deployment

catalog.section: Developing secure agents: Red teaming
catalog.text: Conduct red teaming exercises to identify potential loopholes and unintended behaviour

catalog.section: Developing secure agents: Red teaming
catalog.text: Use capability elicitation techniques to probe for unexpected or emergent abilities, especially any that could create substantial resource or environment risks

catalog.section: Developing secure agents: Red teaming
catalog.text: Implement agent simulation tests, such as multi-agent red teaming or chaos testing.

catalog.section: Developing secure agents: Resilience
catalog.text: Embed agentic AI systems with fail-safe defaults and containment mechanisms that limit the blast radius of unexpected behaviours

catalog.section: Developing secure agents: Resilience
catalog.text: Implement data loss prevention controls specifically tuned to AI agent behaviours

catalog.section: Developing secure agents: Resilience
catalog.text: Implement versioning and rollback mechanisms to safely revert a system to known-good agent behaviours when unpredictability is observed

catalog.section: Developing secure agents: Accountability
catalog.text: Integrate comprehensive artefact logging mechanisms by default

catalog.section: Developing secure agents: Accountability
catalog.text: Integrate unified audit logs for all inter-agent interactions to maintain observability of all agent exchanges

catalog.section: Developing secure agents: Accountability
catalog.text: Use interpretability tools to ensure observability of and reasoning behind agent decisions

catalog.section: Developing secure agents: Accountability
catalog.text: Require specific information referencing for agents that show where key aspects of their response originated from.

catalog.section: Developing secure agents: Manage third-party components
catalog.text: Verify all external third-party components originate from trusted sources and are up to date before inclusion in agentic AI systems

catalog.section: Developing secure agents: Manage third-party components
catalog.text: Maintain a trusted registry of third-party components

catalog.section: Developing secure agents: Manage third-party components
catalog.text: Reference CISA’s A Shared Vision of Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) for Cybersecurity and 2025 Minimum Elements for a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) when procuring agentic AI systems

catalog.section: Developing secure agents: Manage third-party components
catalog.text: Restrict tool use to an approved allow list of tools and versions that are regularly verified as secure

catalog.section: Developing secure agents: Manage third-party components
catalog.text: Verify agent behaviour related to tool usage aligns with documented security policies

catalog.section: Developing secure agents: Manage third-party components
catalog.text: Log agent tool usage and ensure results are captured in system logs in a human-readable format

catalog.section: Developing secure agents: Manage third-party components
catalog.text: Establish trigger-action protocols that automatically restrict agent permissions when unexpected behaviour emerges

catalog.section: Developing secure agents: Manage third-party components
catalog.text: Codify separation of duties by defining roles, such as ‘Orchestrator’, ‘Reader’ and ‘Actuator’ with clear boundaries, consensus mechanisms and delegations expiry

catalog.section: Developing secure agents: Manage third-party components
catalog.text: Implement consensus controls for actions based on risk; use multi agent approval for moderate stakes actions and human in the loop approval in addition to multi agent consensus for high stakes actions

catalog.section: Developing secure agents: Manage third-party components
catalog.text: Prohibit agents from modifying their own privileges or initiating unapproved delegation without explicit expiry timers and recorded grant chains

catalog.section: Developing secure agents: Manage third-party components
catalog.text: Standardise tool descriptions using a consistent format that avoids persuasive language

catalog.section: Deploying agents securely: Threat modelling
catalog.text: Perform realistic threat modelling using up-to-date risk taxonomies for agentic AI systems, such as OWASP GenAI Security Project and MITRE ATLAS™

catalog.section: Deploying agents securely: Threat modelling
catalog.text: Design and implement security controls that address emerging and evolving agent capabilities

catalog.section: Deploying agents securely: Threat modelling
catalog.text: Harmonise agentic AI controls with existing security frameworks, national guidance and allied agreements, such as common Zero Trust principles and the National Institute of Standards and Technology’s Zero Trust Architecture guidance

catalog.section: Deploying agents securely: Threat modelling
catalog.text: Develop and test incident response procedures to detect, contain and recover from agent compromise

catalog.section: Deploying agents securely: Threat modelling
catalog.text: Establish regular third-party reviews of privileged architectures, share actionable intelligence with trusted partners and update risk models to reflect emerging malicious trends

catalog.section: Deploying agents securely: Governance
catalog.text: Implement and maintain governance policies to manage autonomous agents

catalog.section: Deploying agents securely: Governance
catalog.text: Define legal accountability and risk ownership for agentic AI systems in policies

catalog.section: Deploying agents securely: Governance
catalog.text: Upskill the organisation to build AI literacy

catalog.section: Deploying agents securely: Progressive deployment
catalog.text: Implement phased deployment with progressively increasing access and autonomy, limiting the action space where required, such as restricted APIs or sandboxing

catalog.section: Deploying agents securely: Progressive deployment
catalog.text: Use graduated autonomy to incrementally increase agent independence whilst maintaining human oversight and understanding

catalog.section: Deploying agents securely: Progressive deployment
catalog.text: Use continuous evaluation to determine when to expand system scope or when to roll back autonomy and access in response to failures

catalog.section: Deploying agents securely: Secure by default
catalog.text: Set system configurations to fail-safe by default requiring agents to stop and escalate issues to human reviewers in uncertain scenarios

catalog.section: Deploying agents securely: Secure by default
catalog.text: Use error-handling and failover management to reduce the impact of system failures

catalog.section: Deploying agents securely: Secure by default
catalog.text: Implement graceful degradation models so that agents maintain partial functionality even if some functions fail

catalog.section: Deploying agents securely: Guardrails and constraints
catalog.text: Specify clear, constrained objectives with explicit ‘do-not-do’ rules

catalog.section: Deploying agents securely: Guardrails and constraints
catalog.text: Implement guardrails and hard constraints, such as deny lists and API-level safety policies

catalog.section: Deploying agents securely: Guardrails and constraints
catalog.text: Establish declarative safety contracts with constraints and guardrails that agents cannot override

catalog.section: Deploying agents securely: Guardrails and constraints
catalog.text: Apply a layered set of guardrail mechanisms, ranging from anomaly detection and rule-based filtering to specialised machine learning algorithms that detect and filter prohibited behaviour

catalog.section: Deploying agents securely: Guardrails and constraints
catalog.text: Prioritise review of high-risk incidents, including cases where guardrails are triggered or actions are denied by human reviewers

catalog.section: Deploying agents securely: Guardrails and constraints
catalog.text: Deploy a secondary agent to validate new tasks against policy before execution

catalog.section: Deploying agents securely: Isolation
catalog.text: Implement isolation and segmentation to limit blast radius of agent failure scenarios

catalog.section: Deploying agents securely: Isolation
catalog.text: Separate high-risk agents into distinct domains

catalog.section: Deploying agents securely: Isolation
catalog.text: Isolate agents into enclaves with no write access to logs

catalog.section: Operating agents securely: Monitoring and auditing
catalog.text: Employ monitoring tools that enhance human oversight of agentic AI systems

catalog.section: Operating agents securely: Monitoring and auditing
catalog.text: Monitor all agent operations, including internal processes, not just the inputs and outputs

catalog.section: Operating agents securely: Monitoring and auditing
catalog.text: Monitor and log identity and privilege changes and audit regularly for drift, impersonation or misconfiguration

catalog.section: Operating agents securely: Monitoring and auditing
catalog.text: Monitor agent outputs and behaviour for indicators of bias, emerging data drift and other anomalous patterns, including user prompts, tool calls, memory interactions, internal reasoning, decisions made and actions taken

catalog.section: Operating agents securely: Monitoring and auditing
catalog.text: Maintain comprehensive logs and real-time monitoring of live agent behaviour and decision-making

catalog.section: Operating agents securely: Monitoring and auditing
catalog.text: Implement runtime monitoring and anomaly detection using rules or behavioural baselines to identify unusual patterns and trigger alerts or pauses

catalog.section: Operating agents securely: Monitoring and auditing
catalog.text: Establish anomaly detection mechanisms that flag discrepancies between stated intentions and observed behaviours

catalog.section: Operating agents securely: Monitoring and auditing
catalog.text: Use multiple independent monitoring systems that cross-validate agent reports and system logs

catalog.section: Operating agents securely: Monitoring and auditing
catalog.text: Monitor for goal drift by comparing active objectives against approved baseline specifications before execution

catalog.section: Operating agents securely: Monitoring and auditing
catalog.text: Integrate source checks with agent logs to record which tools the system used and what information it retrieved

catalog.section: Operating agents securely: Monitoring and auditing
catalog.text: Implement auditing practices that combine human review with automated analysis of system logs

catalog.section: Operating agents securely: Monitoring and auditing
catalog.text: Support adaptive defences by using monitoring data to enable rapid responses, such as patches based on problems identified in system logs

catalog.section: Operating agents securely: Monitoring and auditing
catalog.text: Use storage-efficient logging methods to manage log volume without losing critical information

catalog.section: Operating agents securely: Monitoring and auditing
catalog.text: Conduct regular security assessments, including penetration testing and red team exercises specifically targeting agentic behaviours

catalog.section: Operating agents securely: Validate outputs
catalog.text: Validate agent outputs by confirming accuracy of critical aspects against multiple sources

catalog.section: Operating agents securely: Validate outputs
catalog.text: Validate agents through cross-checking in environments with redundant agents that validate each other’s outputs

catalog.section: Operating agents securely: Validate outputs
catalog.text: Validate tool responses to prevent malicious or unsafe instructions and standardise tool descriptions to avoid persuasive language

catalog.section: Operating agents securely: Human in the loop
catalog.text: Ensure decisions about when human approval is required are determined by system designers or operators, not delegated to the agentic AI system

catalog.section: Operating agents securely: Human in the loop
catalog.text: Prevent agents from autonomously executing high impact actions or outputs without prior human approval

catalog.section: Operating agents securely: Human in the loop
catalog.text: Insert human-in-the-loop review or approval checkpoints for actions where the cost of error is high, such as system resets, network egress or deletion of critical records.

catalog.section: Operating agents securely: Human in the loop
catalog.text: Quarantine requests to delete logs or audit records until reviewed and approved by a human

catalog.section: Operating agents securely: Human in the loop
catalog.text: Clearly assign responsibility and accountability for errors or adverse outcomes caused by the system

catalog.section: Operating agents securely: Human in the loop
catalog.text: Conduct risk assessments to classify agent actions by potential impact, likelihood and reversibility, and apply appropriate safeguards

catalog.section: Operating agents securely: Performance monitoring
catalog.text: Assess agents’ ability to evade security measures particularly in sensitive or high-impact systems

catalog.section: Operating agents securely: Performance monitoring
catalog.text: Conduct regular assessments of an agent’s ability to bypass safeguards, such as communication barriers, guardrails, monitors, human-in-the-loop processes and input filters

catalog.section: Operating agents securely: Performance monitoring
catalog.text: Use the results from these evaluations to validate existing controls and guide the development of stronger security measures

catalog.section: Operating agents securely: Performance monitoring
catalog.text: Limit agent resource usage by applying controls, such as rate-limit components to interrupt long-running tasks and disrupt malicious workflows

catalog.section: Operating agents securely: Privileges and authentication
catalog.text: Limit privileges of AI agents to the minimum required for its task

catalog.section: Operating agents securely: Privileges and authentication
catalog.text: Restrict scope of privileges to narrowest possible level to allow fine-grained control over allowed actions

catalog.section: Operating agents securely: Privileges and authentication
catalog.text: Implement agent reputation and trust scoring mechanisms and reduce trust levels when anomalous behaviour is detected

catalog.section: Operating agents securely: Privileges and authentication
catalog.text: Require just-in-time credentials for high-impact or privileged actions

catalog.section: Operating agents securely: Privileges and authentication
catalog.text: Verify API caller identity against a user or agent groups

catalog.section: Operating agents securely: Privileges and authentication
catalog.text: Authenticate agents with fresh cryptographic proofs before every privileged call

catalog.section: Operating agents securely: Privileges and authentication
catalog.text: Require cryptographic signing for authorised commands and instructions

catalog.section: Operating agents securely: Privileges and authentication
catalog.text: Apply cryptographic integrity checks for task definitions and constraints

catalog.section: Operating agents securely: Privileges and authentication
catalog.text: Require agents to perform cryptographic attestation where agents must prove that they are running expected and unmodified code

catalog.section: Operating agents securely: Privileges and authentication
catalog.text: Continuously verify identity and authorisation at runtime using a centralised policy decision point for each request

catalog.section: Defend against future risks: Expand threat intelligence through collaboration
catalog.text: Strengthen collaboration between stakeholders to keep pace with evolving threats to agentic AI systems

catalog.section: Defend against future risks: Expand threat intelligence through collaboration
catalog.text: Coordinate with major AI developers and government organisations to compile and maintain threat information

catalog.section: Defend against future risks: Expand threat intelligence through collaboration
catalog.text: Adopt a collaborative security approach, such as those described in CISA’s AI Cybersecurity Collaboration Playbook

catalog.section: Defend against future risks: Expand threat intelligence through collaboration
catalog.text: Implement alerting, data collection and tracking methods for malicious actors and techniques

catalog.section: Defend against future risks: Expand threat intelligence through collaboration
catalog.text: Conduct targeted analysis of threats and capabilities over time to improve situational awareness

catalog.section: Defend against future risks: Expand threat intelligence through collaboration
catalog.text: Harmonise threat intelligence across industries to build shared threat taxonomies that improve threat modelling and support more effective mitigation design

catalog.section: Defend against future risks: Develop robust, agent-specific evaluations
catalog.text: Develop robust evaluation methods to address the gaps in validating agentic AI systems

catalog.section: Defend against future risks: Develop robust, agent-specific evaluations
catalog.text: Generate benchmark datasets to cover new domains and represent realistic deployment contexts

catalog.section: Defend against future risks: Develop robust, agent-specific evaluations
catalog.text: Use evaluation results to validate emerging security practices and identify failure points in agents

catalog.section: Defend against future risks: Develop robust, agent-specific evaluations
catalog.text: Share evaluation findings to strengthen security assessments and support the development of improved security practices across the field

catalog.section: Defend against future risks: Leverage system-theoretic approaches to analyse security
catalog.text: Use system-theoretic approaches to analyse agentic AI systems and identify appropriate security measures

catalog.section: Defend against future risks: Leverage system-theoretic approaches to analyse security
catalog.text: Apply System Theoretic Process Analysis (STPA) and its security extension, STPA for Security (STPA-Sec), to analyse notional or operational systems, identify security issues, assess mission risk and inform potential mitigations

catalog.section: Defend against future risks: Leverage system-theoretic approaches to analyse security
catalog.text: Use Causal Analysis using System Theory (CAST) to investigate security incidents and identify underlying root causes at the system level

catalog.section: Defend against future risks: Leverage system-theoretic approaches to analyse security
catalog.text: Apply STPA and CAST to address safety and security concerns concurrently across agentic AI system lifecycles

catalog.section: Appendix A, cyber security prerequisites: Design
catalog.text: Implement strong authentication by following Secure by Design principles

catalog.section: Appendix A, cyber security prerequisites: Design
catalog.text: Design transparency requirements into the system architecture to enable detection of deception indicators

catalog.section: Appendix A, cyber security prerequisites: Design
catalog.text: Use frameworks, such as zero trust, the Application Security Verification Standard or OAuth2

catalog.section: Appendix A, cyber security prerequisites: Design
catalog.text: Build system infrastructure in a secure, sandboxed environment with encryption, rate limiting and sanitisation

catalog.section: Appendix A, cyber security prerequisites: Design
catalog.text: Apply the principle of least privilege, assigning only the minimum access required for each role

catalog.section: Appendix A, cyber security prerequisites: Design
catalog.text: Limit entitlements to the exact resources, operations and timeframes needed

catalog.section: Appendix A, cyber security prerequisites: Design
catalog.text: Replace static, long-lived secrets with ephemeral credentials that expire when the job is complete

catalog.section: Appendix A, cyber security prerequisites: Design
catalog.text: Dynamically scope privilege for sub-tasks and revoke elevated rights immediately when finished, mitigating scope creep

catalog.section: Appendix A, cyber security prerequisites: Design
catalog.text: Build applications with secure protocols and safe defaults that adhere to communication standards and security policies

catalog.section: Appendix A, cyber security prerequisites: Design
catalog.text: Implement message validation by default so that message components include integrity and freshness checks before use

catalog.section: Appendix A, cyber security prerequisites: Development
catalog.text: Apply secure development principles from U.S. Department of War Enterprise DevSecOps Fundamentals

catalog.section: Appendix A, cyber security prerequisites: Development
catalog.text: Minimise application scope and monitor components for unusual or unexpected behaviour

catalog.section: Appendix A, cyber security prerequisites: Development
catalog.text: Enforce application understanding and only incorporate components into systems that the owner fully understands and accepts the risks of (including possible external effects and processes that it may trigger)

catalog.section: Appendix A, cyber security prerequisites: Development
catalog.text: Refer to frameworks, such as the NIST Secure Software Development Framework or SLSA’s Safeguarding artifact integrity across any software supply chain

catalog.section: Appendix A, cyber security prerequisites: Development
catalog.text: Use supply chain risk management practices for third-party dependencies

catalog.section: Appendix A, cyber security prerequisites: Development
catalog.text: Apply existing governance and organisational management policies

catalog.section: Appendix A, cyber security prerequisites: Development
catalog.text: Conduct threat modelling using frameworks, such as OWASP Top 10:2025, MITRE ATT&CK® and MITRE D3FEND™ and use the results to inform mitigations tailored to the operational environment

catalog.section: Appendix A, cyber security prerequisites: Development
catalog.text: Plan and regularly test incident response plans and teams
